stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Nvidia has released the RTX Spark N1X, a new high-performing Arm-based SoC for laptops and small desktops.
The processor is positioned as a direct competitor to offerings from Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm.
The review focuses on real-world performance testing of laptops equipped with this new 'superchip'.

stories.title: Meta’s new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta's updated terms of service grant it permission to crawl and scrape content from associated websites, including online news publishers.
The new terms explicitly allow Meta to use this external content for purposes such as 'develop, improve, research,' and 'train' its AI models.
This policy change, effective October 30th, raises significant concerns regarding data usage rights and intellectual property for news organizations.

stories.title: The iPhone Duo is now available to preorder at $1,999
stories.author: Sheena Vasani
bullet_points: Apple has officially unveiled its first foldable iPhone, dubbed the 'iPhone Duo'.
The device is available for preorder starting at a price point of $1,999.
The iPhone Duo features a 5.4-inch outer screen and was announced alongside the iPhone 18 Pro.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI for AI (AI4AI) and the concept of recursive self-improvement (RSI).
MLExpert utilizes workflow-driven systems and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation autonomously.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research proposes MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI for AI (AI4AI) and the concept of recursive self-improvement (RSI).
The model utilizes workflow-driven orchestration and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and context gathering.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs and faster response times.
The updated engine also demonstrates improved memory efficiency when running models.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
Addresses the gap between controlled agent benchmarks and the ambiguity of live customer environments.
Comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 real-world customer scenarios across 18 sectors.

stories.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
stories.author: Laurent Itti
bullet_points: Introduction of 3DCodeVerse, a new research ecosystem designed to enable coding agents to generate editable and verifiable 3D content.
The ecosystem includes a large-scale, high-quality dataset of executable 3D code, specifically 3DCodeVerse-2M.
It provides a coding harness focused on spatial reasoning and automated verification for 3D coding tasks.

stories.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
stories.author: Tat-Seng Chua
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of 'goal drift' in complex LLM agents and multi-agent systems.
Proposes a novel 'steering agent' designed to supervise execution in real-time.
This mechanism actively corrects system behavior when agents deviate from the intended overall goal during long-horizon tasks.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is offered for free for a limited time via Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within a cloud environment.
Fly.io provides the cloud infrastructure for safely running these AI agents.
The integration focuses on enhancing the safety and deployment of AI agents.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: A fake WhatsApp clone is showing up before the real version on the Play Store
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: A fraudulent WhatsApp clone is appearing on the Google Play Store.
The fake app is being promoted in a 'sponsored' slot above the legitimate WhatsApp.
The scam application has already accumulated over 500,000 downloads.

stories.title: iPhone Duo orders are already delayed into 2027
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Preorders for the unreleased 'iPhone Duo' immediately faced delivery delays.
Delivery estimates jumped to late January shortly after the 8 AM ET preorder launch.
The foldable device is scheduled for a physical store launch on October 23rd.

stories.title: Blue Origin is going all in on the New Glenn rocket
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Blue Origin is heavily investing in the New Glenn rocket program.
The infrastructure development aims to enable high flight cadence.
The goal is to support multiple rocket flights weekly by the end of the decade.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in robotic agents.
Investigates how embodied agents can follow user preferences in zero-shot learning scenarios, crucial for household robotics.

stories.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
stories.author: Mikhail D. Lukin
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Large Language Models (LLMs) to discover advanced quantum circuits.
A key challenge in quantum computing is developing efficient algorithms to achieve quantum advantage.
The optimization process in quantum computing is complicated by constraints like reversibility, unlike classical computation.

stories.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
stories.author: Yejin Choi
bullet_points: Introduces T2-Z, a method for Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents in robotic world models.
Addresses the challenge of robots needing to predict outcomes based on unobservable environmental factors (e.g., friction, mass).
Augments existing robotic world models with a learnable latent variable to condition world predictions on hidden environmental properties.

stories.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces CoDA, a framework designed to improve robotic learning by co-evolving data engines and action policies.
Addresses the limitation of generative simulations by focusing on creating physically valid environments that specifically target policy failures.
Utilizes a shared heterogeneous memory to track environment construction, policy errors, and learning progress for targeted supervision.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses routing exploration challenges in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It examines the interplay between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
A core dilemma identified is how shared experts can reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: GeoState addresses a key limitation in 3D world modeling where geometry features from foundation models are view-dependent.
The proposed method introduces a view-decoupled geometry representation to separate scene dynamics from camera-induced variations.
This decoupling aims to significantly improve the predictive accuracy of 3D world models by providing a cleaner state evolution.

stories.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
stories.author: Ruoshi Liu
bullet_points: Introduces DSP (Dexterity from supervised play), a framework for teaching robots complex manipulation.
The system uses behavior cloning on short human demonstrations to initialize a play policy.
This policy then guides autonomous data collection to train a world model, which is used with MPC for control.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in embodied agents.
Investigates how robotic policies adhere to user preferences, even in zero-shot learning scenarios.

stories.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
stories.author: Bernie Wang
bullet_points: PathFM is a new trajectory-based forecasting model designed to address limitations in current time series foundation models.
Unlike existing models that predict marginal quantiles, PathFM explicitly models the dependence structure of future multivariate trajectories.
The model leverages flow matching to improve forecasting accuracy for trajectory-dependent metrics like cumulative demand and peak load.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the 'exploration dilemma' in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It focuses on the interaction between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
The research suggests that shared experts can limit the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: GeoState addresses a key limitation in 3D world modeling where geometry features from foundation models are view-dependent.
The proposed method introduces a view-decoupled geometry representation to separate scene dynamics from camera-induced variations.
This decoupling aims to improve the predictability of state evolution in complex 3D environments.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: Addresses a core limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding representation design.
Proposes using 'complementary representations' to allow models to selectively preserve or factor out specific temporal information.
Aims to move beyond the fixed inductive bias imposed by single representation approaches in TSLMs.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research introduces a distinction between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are defined as knowledge that supports generalization beyond its initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this distinction by manipulating existing knowledge relations to test generalization capabilities.

stories.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces OmniVerifier-C1, a new decomposed graded verifier for generative world modeling.
Moves beyond traditional binary (True/False) verification by providing continuous, fine-grained scores.
Aims to enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex, rule-governed multimodal scenarios.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
The benchmark moves beyond simple, well-defined tasks by incorporating ambiguous requirements and live system constraints.
It comprises 95 end-to-end delivery tasks sourced from 20 customer scenarios across 18 different industry sectors.

stories.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
stories.author: Pratham Yogish Maliya
bullet_points: The research investigates 'evaluation awareness' in LLMs—the tendency for models to behave differently during safety testing than in real-world use.
Existing studies on this phenomenon have been heavily focused on English, neglecting the vast linguistic diversity of the world.
This work specifically tests four instruction-tuned models across Indic languages, addressing a significant gap in multilingual AI safety research.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding how they represent temporal data.
It proposes using 'complementary representations' as a design principle to improve time-series reasoning.
This approach aims to allow models to preserve necessary information while factoring out irrelevant variation, overcoming fixed inductive biases.

stories.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM applications for scientific ideation: optimizing for idea quality often neglects idea diversity.
The study focuses on 'document-grounded ideation,' aiming to generate sets of ideas that are both high-quality and significantly distinct from one another.
This work contributes to the methodology of using LLMs in the early, creative stages of the scientific research pipeline.

stories.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: Addresses a gap in multi-agent systems by jointly learning individual agent policies and collective self-orchestration.
Introduces Market-Based Post-Training (MPT) as a novel framework for decentralized agent swarms.
Agents utilize a bidding mechanism to express willingness to participate in the swarm's tasks.

stories.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
stories.author: Ricardo Rei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need to evaluate AI chatbots used for mental health support.
Identifies limitations in current evaluation methods, such as overly simplistic synthetic patient interactions and opaque judging rubrics.
Introduces MindEval2, a new framework using clinically grounded patients and rubrics for more rigorous LLM evaluation in this domain.

stories.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
stories.author: Yue Zhao
bullet_points: Introduces Grid-Bench, a new executable benchmark designed to test LLMs on spatial reasoning.
The benchmark evaluates LLMs' ability to predict the resulting state of discrete worlds after a sequence of spatial operations.
Tests involve transforming 2D, 3D, and 4D grids using various families of spatial instructions.

stories.title: Big Fish: Exploiting a 37-Year-Old Kernel Bug in OpenBSD
stories.author: rs_rs_rs_rs_rs
bullet_points: A significant vulnerability was discovered in the OpenBSD kernel.
The bug is notable for its age, dating back 37 years.
The story highlights the ongoing security challenges in legacy or established operating systems.

stories.title: Show HN: Gemini 4 Argon plays StarCraft
stories.author: __cayenne__
bullet_points: A new benchmark, StarSkirmish Bench, has been introduced to test LLMs' ability to play StarCraft.
The benchmark evaluates flagship models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Muse.
The models achieve this by writing code to control the game, indicating a focus on complex reasoning and execution.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on AI-assisted kernel contributions
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds is discussing the integration and implications of AI assistance in kernel development.
The topic touches upon the future of open-source software contribution workflows.
The discussion is situated within the Linux kernel community, a highly influential area of computing.
